claims.text: A Pt-based catalyst functionalized with a thin, uniform layer of TiO2 nanoparticles will exhibit enhanced catalytic activity toward HER and HOR.
A Pt-based catalyst functionalized with a thin, uniform layer of TiO2 nanoparticles will exhibit enhanced durability toward HER and HOR.
A thin, uniform TiO2 nanoparticle layer can be deposited on the Pt-based catalyst by 10 ALD cycles at 200°C.
Surface TiO2 nanoparticles modify the surface properties of the Pt-based catalyst.
Surface TiO2 nanoparticles enhance the catalytic activity of the Pt-based catalyst.
TiO2 nanoparticles increase the catalyst surface area.
TiO2 nanoparticles improve charge transfer in the catalyst.
TiO2 nanoparticles reduce the adsorption of poisoning species.
Increased surface area, improved charge transfer, and reduced adsorption of poisoning species lead to enhanced HER and HOR activity and durability.
Under the stated electrochemical conditions, functionalization will increase exchange current density by 30% relative to the unfunctionalized Pt-based catalyst.
Under the stated electrochemical conditions, functionalization will reduce the Tafel slope by 50% relative to the unfunctionalized Pt-based catalyst.
The functionalized catalyst will remain stable for more than 1000 hours.
TiO2 functionalization will be effective only when the layer is uniform and thinner than 5 nm.
